pitch.body:
SLIDE 1 - THE LEGACY GAP
A person can live for eighty years and be remembered by a birth date, a death date and a folder of photographs. What they chose, believed, regretted and loved survives only in the stories someone keeps. Think about how your parents met. You know the short version, but who made the first move? Mom and Dad might not even agree. Each person holds one piece, and when it isn't passed on, it's gone. That is the legacy gap. Seventy-four percent of adult children want to know more about their parents' lives before parenthood, but only thirty-seven percent knew their mother's early life. Families care. They just keep missing the moment. Photo albums keep the pictures but lose the life behind them. Memoir services like Storyworth send weekly prompts toward a book, and the gift turns into homework for parents. Habits take a median of sixty-six days of daily repetition. Weekly prompts get about ten tries in that window, and once the book is printed, the purpose is gone.

SLIDE 2 - A STORY
Meet A Story, an AI biographer that calls your loved ones and helps them tell their stories in their own voice. They answer the phone and talk. A Story does the asking and follows what they actually say instead of a script. Every call remembers the last one, picks up unfinished stories, and lets each memory shape the next question, so it becomes a habit instead of a project. And because one person only remembers their part, every relative can join, adding photos, corrections or their own version of the same day, each credited to them. A photo can raise a question no one thought to ask, and a missing detail goes to the relative most likely to know it. When the family wants something physical, any chapter becomes a printed book with the original voices one scan away, and the story keeps going after it's printed.

SLIDE 3 - BUILT WITH FAMILIES
We're three founders: Daniel leads product and fundraising, Bao leads operations and partnerships, and I lead brand and how we reach families. The product works end to end, calls to archive to billing. Our first version brought in fifty leads. We chose ten families for a private beta, watched how they actually used it, and redesigned before scaling. Five more families are waiting to join as paying customers. Families pay one hundred nineteen dollars a year, or two twenty-nine for a family plan; relatives join free, and books start at sixty-nine. Next is our public launch and holiday gifting campaign, where we'll measure what matters: do storytellers come back for another call, and do relatives' contributions spark the next conversation. We're building A Story so that "I meant to ask" doesn't become "I wish I had."

BEFORE YOU USE IT
1. Prices: Oct 14 says $119 / $229 / books from $69, but Sep 30 notes say a $1 and $30 plan rollout. Approve one under Decisions (pricing proposal) and fix Slide 3.
2. Traction (50 leads, 10 beta families, 5 waiting paying) is owner-reported, not yet approved company truth. Keep the exact numbers you can defend.
3. Survey stats (74% / 37%): add the source to the slide footnote. The 79% regret figure was dropped for time; add it back only with its source.
4. 66 days is the median from Lally et al. (2010), European Journal of Social Psychology. Cite it.
5. Hope College interest was cut for time. Mention it in Q&A only as interest, not a partnership.
6. Give Nhi one concrete credibility line (something she built, marketed or led), as the Oct 14 notes ask.

Length: about 3 minutes at a steady 150 words per minute. Rehearse with the timer; the word count is an estimate.
